newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Germany's Kinkel urges Bulgaria to reform, win aid.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kinkel urges Bulgaria to reform, win aid.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel warned on Friday Bulgaria was on the brink of economic disaster and should carry out rapid and radical reform to avoid deeper crisis and to win foreign aid.

"Bulgaria is on the brink of economic catastrophe...Large numbers of the population live below the poverty line...Many people are incapable of buying food and basic goods without external help," said Kinkel in a statement released by the German Embassy in Sofia.
"The interim government must begin radical economic reform. Quick reform is the only way to free former socialist economies from inherited burdens."

The Balkan country is suffering an unprecedented crisis precipitated by delays in reforms over the past seven years. Mismanagement by the previous Socialist administration and asset stripping of banks and factories have left the economy in disarray.

"The European Union...is called upon to show assistance for resolving the crisis and for the survival of a neighbouring European country. Bulgaria is an associate member of the European Union and has prospects for future membership," said Kinkel, adding that he would visit Bulgaria soon.

The European Union has earmarked 20 million ecus ($23 million) to support 450,000 households with a per capita income of less than 3,250 levs a month, and residents of some 570 social institutions. The payments will begin in March.

In the beginning of February, after month-long mass protests President Petar Stoyanov mediated a deal providing for an early general election on April 19, dissolved parliament and named a caretaker cabinet.
The caretaker government, battling an acute fuel and grain crisis in its first three weeks in office, raised fuel, power, heating and telephone charges in a first move to liberalise prices.
